recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-16950 unless a future work group decision changes primitive integer range semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-16950 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request raised against STU3 datatypes. It asked whether unsignedInt and positiveInt were specializations of the 32-bit integer type, independent unsigned widths, or otherwise size-limited, and the final resolution was to note that all integers are constrained to 32-bit numbers.
initial_application: The issue was applied by git-svn commit 2f25071c64f0b50b23e620ac55e77e794ab692a7, matching the Jira comment for svn 14286. That commit changed source/datatypes.html to give integer the signed 32-bit range and to give unsignedInt and positiveInt explicit upper bounds of 2,147,483,647.
additional_context: The current build scope routes primitive type pages through datatypes.html, and source/fhir.ini marks integer, positiveInt, and unsignedInt as ranged primitive types. Later datatype-page refactors preserved the same range semantics. The active primitive spreadsheet models unsignedInt and positiveInt as based on integer and no longer has a positiveInt regex that allows a plus sign. Community and related-issue searches found no conflicting evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was needed. The current source says integer is limited to -2,147,483,648..2,147,483,647, positiveInt is 1..2,147,483,647, and unsignedInt is 0..2,147,483,647.
